Prepare anchored pairwise DNA differences

Source: R/alignseq-data.R
alignseq_data.Rd

Convert two already aligned DNA strings into an inspectable table for geom_alignseq(). No alignment is inferred. Coordinates are one-based base centres; gaps do not consume genomic bases and are anchored at the adjacent half-base boundary. Insertions and deletions describe the other sequence relative to the explicitly named reference, not evolutionary direction.

Usage

alignseq_data(
  aligned,
  anchors,
  reference,
  regions = NULL,
  details = NULL,
  flank = 3
)

Arguments

aligned

Named character vector of exactly two equal-length aligned DNA strings. Use - for gaps. IUPAC ambiguity codes are retained and marked ambiguous, rather than called verified substitutions.

anchors

Data frame with one row per sequence and columns sequence, start, strand. start is the genomic coordinate of the first non-gap character in the supplied orientation; strand is + or -. Strings on the minus strand must already be oriented for comparison. Optional track, chr, and y columns control annotation-panel placement. Defaults are the sequence name, NA, and 1, respectively. Anchors describe contiguous DNA, not spliced transcript sequence.

reference

Name of the reference in aligned.

regions

Selected reference-coordinate windows: a numeric start/end pair or a data frame with start, end. NULL retains the whole alignment. A gap column is selected by its half-base reference anchor.

details

Explicit reference-coordinate windows for DNA callouts, in the same format as regions. NULL adds no callouts. Nearby windows merge when their expanded alignment-column ranges overlap or touch. Detail is restricted to the selected regions and split wherever columns are omitted.

flank

Nonnegative integer number of aligned columns added on each side of each detail window.

Value

A data frame, one row per sequence per selected aligned column, with x, y, track, position (NA at gaps), column, base, event_type, event_id, event_length, reference_x, and detail_id. Contiguous indel columns form one event; each substitution is one event. Matching columns have no event ID. Rows also retain both aligned bases and sequence names for matched-column comparison. Empty selections return a typed empty table.

Examples

dna <- c(human = "AC-GTAC", chimp = "ATCG-AC")
anchors <- data.frame(sequence = names(dna), start = c(100, 900), strand = "+")
d <- alignseq_data(dna, anchors, reference = "human",
  details = c(101, 103), flank = 1)
ggplot2::ggplot() + geom_alignseq(data = d) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~track, scales = "free_x")
